    # =========================================================================
# web/views/registration.py: "Create a patient account": a patient who does not
# have an account yet creates it themselves. PUBLIC routes (one has no account yet,
# by definition):
#
#   POST /register/access     "Create a patient account" button of the
#                             authentication page: checks the captcha of THIS
#                             page, then opens the form
#   GET  /register            the form
#   POST /register            the creation, then back to the login page
#
# The path is protected against robots by ONE captcha, that of the
# authentication page:
#   1. the "Create a patient account" button sends the login form to
#      /register/access; if the captcha is typed correctly, the server issues a
#      pass (see security/registration_pass.py);
#   2. without a valid pass, /register sends back to the
#      authentication page (decorator @registration_pass_required);
#   3. the pass is consumed on creation: a solved captcha allows the creation of
#      ONE account;
#   4. in addition, the number of accounts created per hour and per IP address is limited
#      (see security/limiter.py).
#
# The account created is exactly the one the ADMIN would create from the "Patients" page
# (same method of the business layer: add_client), except that the patient
# CHOOSES their login and password (required, with confirmation).
# =========================================================================

from urllib.parse import urlencode

from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.urls import reverse
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _, ngettext
from django.views.decorators.http import require_http_methods, require_POST

from business.errors import BusinessError
from security import captchas, limiter, registration_pass
from security.registration_pass import registration_pass_required

from .. import utils
from ..application import application
from ..forms import RegistrationForm
from .persons import BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS


# the "too many accounts created" message, in the singular or in the plural
def too_many_accounts(minutes: int) -> str:
    return ngettext(
        "Too many accounts have been created from your connection. Try again in %(minutes)d minute.",
        "Too many accounts have been created from your connection. Try again in %(minutes)d minutes.",
        minutes) % {"minutes": minutes}


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /register/access   fields: captcha_id, captcha (those of the
# authentication page; login and password, also sent, are ignored)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def access(request):
    ip = utils.ip(request)
    # too many accounts created recently from this address: no point going further
    minutes = limiter.registration_block_minutes(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        messages.error(request, too_many_accounts(minutes))
        return redirect("login")
    # missing or wrong captcha: back to the authentication page, with a
    # new image (a failure counts as a login failure)
    if not captchas.verify(request.POST.get("captcha_id", ""), request.POST.get("captcha", "")):
        limiter.login_failure(ip, "")
        messages.error(request, _("To create an account, first type the characters shown in the image "
                                  "correctly, then click \"Create a patient account\"."))
        return redirect("login")
    # correct captcha: the pass is issued and the form is opened
    return registration_pass.issue(redirect("registration"))


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /register: the form; POST /register: the creation. The
# pass has been checked BEFORE the call of the view (@registration_pass_required).
# The form validates ALL the input (fields and password confirmation):
# the user corrects all their errors in one go
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
@registration_pass_required
def registration(request):
    if request.method == "GET":
        return page(request, RegistrationForm(initial={"title": "Mr"}))
    form = RegistrationForm(request.POST)
    if not form.is_valid():
        return page(request, form)
    ip = utils.ip(request)
    # 1. too many accounts created recently from this address?
    minutes = limiter.registration_block_minutes(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        return page(request, form, too_many_accounts(minutes))
    # 2. the creation (client + USER account, in a transaction)
    data = form.person_data()
    try:
        application().add_client(data)
    except BusinessError as e:
        # login or first + last name already taken: the pass remains valid
        return page(request, form, e.message, BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS.get(e.code, []))
    # 3. the pass has been used: it will not allow the creation of a 2nd account
    registration_pass.consume(request.COOKIES.get(registration_pass.COOKIE))
    limiter.registration_success(ip)
    # 4. back to the login page, login pre-filled
    messages.success(request, _("Your account has been created. You can now log in with "
                                "the login %(login)s.") % {"login": data.login})
    url = f"{reverse('login')}?{urlencode({'login': data.login})}"
    return registration_pass.clear_cookie(redirect(url))


# the form; a refused form: the 422 code
def page(request, form, error=None, invalid_fields=()):
    refused = error is not None or (form.is_bound and bool(form.errors))
    return render(request, "registration.html", {
        "page_title": _("Create a patient account"),
        "form": form.flag(invalid_fields), "error": error,
    }, status=422 if refused else 200)

    The patient creates a patient account themselves. The flow is protected by a CAPTCHA, the same one used on the login page.

    • Lines 59–75: The “Create a patient account” button on the login page submits the login form to this address (which later becomes the template [login.html]). If too many accounts have been created recently from this address (IP), there is no need to proceed further. If the CAPTCHA is missing or incorrect: return to the login page with a new image and a message; the failure counts as a failed login attempt (with an empty username). If the CAPTCHA is correct: a token is stored in a cookie, and the user is redirected to the form;
    • lines 84–91: the form. The [@registration_pass_required] decorator (line 85) checks the token before calling the view. The order of the decorators matters: the one closest to the function is applied first; [require_http_methods], placed above, therefore rejects a prohibited method before any other checks. The form validates the entire input, including password confirmation: the user sees all their errors at once;
    • Lines 92–111: account creation. The client and their account are created using the same business-logic method as for the administrator ([add_client]); only the username and password are chosen by the patient. If a username or a homonym is already taken: return to the form without consuming the token. Creating an account consumes the token (one solved CAPTCHA equals one account), counts toward the hourly limit, and redirects to the login page with the username pre-filled (parameter [?login=...], generated by [urlencode]), along with a success message. The pass cookie is cleared.

    # =========================================================================
# web/views/area.py: the PERSONAL pages of the patient (USER role), the one they
# see just after logging in:
#
#   GET  /my-area                  home page: [Manage my account], [View a
#                                  schedule], and their upcoming appointment
#   POST /my-area/cancel           cancels THEIR appointment
#   GET  /my-account               update form of their account
#   POST /my-account               update
#   POST /my-account/delete        deletion of the account (and of its appointments)
#
# Golden rule of this module: the patient concerned is ALWAYS the one of the token
# (utils.connected_patient), never an identifier sent by the browser. A
# patient can therefore neither see, nor modify, nor cancel what belongs to another
# patient, even by building their requests themselves.
#
# Any update or deletion of the account requires the CURRENT password:
# someone who found a session left open could neither change the
# password, nor delete the account. The current password errors are
# counted as login failures (same limit).
#
# Security: all these URLs are reserved to the USER role (rule ^/my- of
# security/access.py).
# =========================================================================

from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _, ngettext
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_http_methods, require_POST

from business.errors import BusinessError
from models.models import Client
from security import auth, limiter

from .. import utils
from ..application import application
from ..forms import MyAccountForm
from ..view_models import AppointmentView
from .schedule import schedule_url
from .persons import BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-area
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_GET
def area(request):
    patient = utils.connected_patient(request)
    appointments = [AppointmentView(
        a.id,
        utils.format_day(a.day),
        a.slot.time_range(),
        a.slot.doctor.label(),
        # link to the schedule of the doctor that day: the patient sees their name there
        schedule_url(a.slot.doctor_id, a.day))
        for a in application().get_client_upcoming_appointments(patient.id)]
    return render(request, "area.html", {"page_title": _("My area"),
                                         "patient": patient.label(), "appointments": appointments})


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-area/cancel   field: appointmentId
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def cancel_appointment(request):
    patient = utils.connected_patient(request)
    appointment_id = utils.positive_integer(request.POST.get("appointmentId"))
    appointment = application().get_appointment_by_id(appointment_id) if appointment_id is not None else None
    # an appointment that does not exist, and that of ANOTHER patient, get the same
    # answer: nothing is revealed about the appointments of the others
    if appointment is None or appointment.client_id != patient.id:
        messages.error(request, _("This appointment does not exist (any more)."))
    else:
        application().delete_appointment(appointment)
        messages.success(request, _("Appointment cancelled."))
    return redirect("area")


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-account: the form, pre-filled with the values of the patient;
# POST /my-account: the update
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
def account(request):
    patient = utils.connected_patient(request)
    if request.method == "GET":
        return page(request, MyAccountForm(initial={
            "title": patient.title, "first_name": patient.first_name, "last_name": patient.last_name,
            "login": patient.account.login, "version": patient.version}))
    form = MyAccountForm(request.POST)
    if not form.is_valid():
        return page(request, form)
    # the current password; wrong: the message goes UNDER the field (an error added
    # to the field by add_error), and at the bottom of the page
    error = check_current_password(request, patient, form.cleaned_data["current_password"])
    if error is not None:
        form.add_error("current_password", error)
        return page(request, form, error)
    try:
        client = application().edit_client(patient.id, form.person_data())
    except BusinessError as e:
        return page(request, form, e.message, BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS.get(e.code, []))
    # the login and the displayed name are IN the token: a new one is issued, otherwise
    # the navigation bar would keep the old name
    messages.success(request, _("Your account has been updated."))
    return auth.set_token(redirect("area"), client.account)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-account/delete   field: current_password
# The account, the client and ALL their appointments disappear together, then the
# patient is logged out.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def delete_account(request):
    patient = utils.connected_patient(request)
    error = check_current_password(request, patient, request.POST.get("current_password", ""))
    if error is not None:
        messages.error(request, error)
        return redirect("account")
    application().delete_client(patient.id)
    messages.success(request, _("Your account has been deleted."))
    return auth.clear_token(redirect("login"))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions
# the account page; a refused form: the 422 code
def page(request, form, error=None, invalid_fields=()):
    refused = error is not None or (form.is_bound and bool(form.errors))
    return render(request, "account.html", {
        "page_title": _("Manage my account"),
        "form": form.flag(invalid_fields), "error": error,
    }, status=422 if refused else 200)


# None if the current password is correct; otherwise the error message
def check_current_password(request, patient: Client, password: str) -> str | None:
    ip = utils.ip(request)
    login = patient.account.login
    minutes = limiter.login_block_minutes(ip, login)
    if minutes > 0:
        return ngettext("Too many failed attempts. Try again in %(minutes)d minute.",
                        "Too many failed attempts. Try again in %(minutes)d minutes.",
                        minutes) % {"minutes": minutes}
    if not password or auth.validate(login, password) is None:
        limiter.login_failure(ip, login)
        return _("Incorrect current password.")
    return None

    The patient’s personal pages. The golden rule of this module: the patient in question is always the one associated with the token ([utils.connected_patient]), never an identifier sent by the browser. A patient cannot therefore view, modify, or cancel information belonging to another patient, even if they generate their own requests.

    • Lines 46–58: My area: the patient’s name and their upcoming appointments, formatted ([AppointmentView]), each with a link to the doctor’s schedule for that day. The function [schedule_url] is part of the calendar module (line 39, [from .schedule import schedule_url]);
    • lines 64–76: the cancellation of his appointment. Both a nonexistent appointment and another patient’s appointment receive the same response: no information is disclosed about other patients’ appointments (not even their existence);
    • lines 83–92: the “Manage my account” form, pre-filled with the patient’s information, and its submission;
    • lines 95–106: the modification. Any modification requires the current password: someone who found a session left open would be unable to change the password or do anything else. If the current password is incorrect, the form is redisplayed, with the message below the field and at the bottom of the page. [add_error(field, message)] adds an error to a field, as if validation had detected it (example 19). After the modification, a new token is generated: the login and the displayed name are included in the token, and the navigation bar would otherwise retain the old name until the next login;
    • lines 114–123: deletion of the account, the client, and all their appointments, using the same business-logic method as for the administrator. This second form on the page is hand-coded (a single field: the current password). The patient is then logged out (the token cookie is cleared);
    • lines 137–148: Verification of the current password. This is subject to the attempt limiter, just like a login: without this, someone with an open session could try thousands of passwords via the “Manage my account” form and discover the correct one.

    <!doctype html>
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/layout.html
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  The PARENT template of all the pages (see example 15): each page
  (schedule.html, login.html...) EXTENDS it ({% extends %}) and fills its
  [content] block.

  Django ESCAPES everything it displays with {{ ... }} (the characters < > & " '
  become &lt; &gt;...): protection against HTML injection through an entered
  name, for example. To insert HTML as is, it must be requested
  explicitly (safe filter, see fragments/captcha.html).

  Messages: a success is displayed at the TOP of the page, an error at the BOTTOM, on a light
  pink background (success_zone and error_zone tags, see web/templatetags/rdv.py).

  The template shares the variables of the page: [page_title] (the title of the
  page, passed on by the view, already translated). LANGUAGE_CODE: the language of the
  request (see web/middleware.py).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load static i18n rdv %}
<html lang="{{ LANGUAGE_CODE }}">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>{{ page_title }} - RdvMedecins</title>
  {# static: the URL of a file of the static folder #}
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'lib/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css' %}">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'css/styles.css' %}">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-4">
    {% include "fragments/navbar.html" %}
    {% success_zone %}
    <main>
      {% block content %}{% endblock %}
    </main>
    {% error_zone %}
  </div>
  {# the "Are you sure?" dialog, hidden as long as it is not needed #}
  {% include "fragments/confirmation.html" %}
  <script src="{% static 'js/app.js' %}"></script>
</body>
</html>

    The parent template for all pages (Example 15): each page extends it ([{% extends "layout.html" %}]) and fills in its [content] block (line 38).

    • Line 23: the tag libraries used: [static] (static files), [i18n] (translations, Example 22), and [rdv], ours (web layer, above). A parent template does not pass its libraries on to the templates that extend it: each page loads the ones it needs;
    • line 24: the page’s language, [fr] or [en]: the active language of the request, set by the [SetLanguage] middleware;
    • line 28: the page title, already translated by the view, which passes it in the variable [page_title];
    • lines 30–31: the [{% static %}] tag renders the URL from a file in the [static] folder (Example 15);
    • lines 35–40: the navigation bar, the success messages at the top of the page, the page content, and the error area at the bottom of the page. The navigation bar snippet is inserted by [{% include %}] (Example 15): it accesses the page’s variables. The two message areas are the inclusion tags from [web/templatetags/rdv.py];
    • lines 43–44: the “Are you sure?” window, hidden until needed, and the script that displays it.

    The header comment (lines 2–22) is a [{% comment %}] tag: a template comment that can span multiple lines ([{# ... #}] fits on a single line, example 14). It is written after [<!doctype html>]: the first line of the sent page must be the document type declaration. The DTL escapes everything it displays using [{{ ... }}] (Example 14): a user-entered name containing HTML ([<script>]) is displayed as-is, without being interpreted. This prevents HTML (XSS) from being injected effortlessly into all pages.

    {% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/navbar.html - the navigation bar.

  Title, FR/EN, role, name, logout - and the menu, whose entries depend
  on the role: they are computed by the context processor web/contexts.py
  (variable menu), with, for each one, its URL, its label, and whether it is the one
  of the current page ("active" class).

  user: the logged-in user, or None (see web/contexts.py).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand-sm navbar-dark bg-primary rounded mb-4 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand mb-0">RdvMedecins</span>

  <ul class="navbar-nav me-auto">
    {% for entry in menu %}
    <li class="nav-item">
      <a class="nav-link{% if entry.active %} active{% endif %}" href="{{ entry.url }}">{{ entry.label }}</a>
    </li>
    {% endfor %}
  </ul>

  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
    {# FR / EN: simple links (GET /language/fr), the active language highlighted #}
    {% get_available_languages as languages %}
    <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" aria-label="FR / EN">
      {% for code, name in languages %}
      <a class="btn {% if code == LANGUAGE_CODE %}btn-light{% else %}btn-outline-light{% endif %}"
         href="{% url 'language' code %}">{{ code|upper }}</a>
      {% endfor %}
    </div>

    {% if user %}
    <span class="badge text-bg-light text-primary">{{ user.role }}</span>
    <span class="text-white">{{ user.name }}</span>
    {# logout is a POST: a form reduced to its button (and to the anti-CSRF token) #}
    <form method="post" action="{% url 'logout' %}" class="m-0">
      {% csrf_token %}
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-light">{% translate "Log out" %}</button>
    </form>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
</nav>

    The navigation bar. It simply displays what the [web/contexts.py] context processor has prepared: the logged-in user ([user]), and the menu items ([menu]), which depend on the role.

    • lines 17–23: the menu, with each entry having its own URL and label; the [active] class of [Bootstrap] highlights the entry for the currently displayed page;
    • Lines 27–32: the FR / EN buttons, simple links ([/language/fr]), with the active language highlighted. [{% get_available_languages as languages %}] (library [i18n]) stores the setting [LANGUAGES]—a list of (code, name) pairs—in the variable [languages], which the loop unpacks ([{% for code, name in languages %}]); the filter [upper] capitalizes the code. [{% url 'language' code %}] creates URL for a route that has a parameter (example 15);
    • Lines 35–43: For a logged-in user, their role, name, and the logout button. Logout is a request for POST: a form reduced to just its button, with its anti-CSRF token ([{% csrf_token %}], Example 21).

    {% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/confirmation.html - the "Are you sure?" modal dialog
  (see example 21).

  It replaces the window.confirm() box of the browser, which can neither be
  styled nor translated (its buttons stay in the language of the browser, not
  in that of the page).

  A SINGLE dialog for the whole page, hidden (d-none) at first. Its labels
  are translated here, by the server, like the rest of the page; the small script
  static/js/app.js merely displays it, puts in it the message specific to the
  form (data-confirmation attribute), and sends the form if
  the user confirms.
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<div id="confirmation-modal" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
       aria-labelledby="confirmation-modal-title" aria-describedby="confirmation-modal-message">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title" id="confirmation-modal-title">{% translate "Confirmation" %}</h5>
          <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-action="no" aria-label="{% translate 'Close' %}"></button>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="confirmation-modal-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          {# "No, go back" rather than "Cancel": the question is sometimes "Cancel this appointment?" #}
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="no">{% translate "No, go back" %}</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="yes">{% translate "Yes, confirm" %}</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

    The “Are you sure?” modal window from Example 21, which replaces the browser’s [window.confirm()] dialog box: this dialog box does not format correctly, and its buttons remain in the browser’s language, not the page’s language. A single window for the entire page, initially hidden (class [d-none] derived from [Bootstrap]); its labels are translated by the server, just like the rest of the page. The [static/js/app.js] script displays it, places the message from the form to be confirmed inside it (its [data-confirmation] attribute), and submits the form if the user confirms. The "Cancel" button is labeled “No, go back” rather than “Cancel”: the question is sometimes “Cancel this appointment?”, and a “Cancel” button would be ambiguous in that context. The attributes [role="alertdialog"], [aria-modal], [aria-labelledby], and [aria-describedby] describe the window to screen readers: a dialog box awaiting a response, its title, and its message.

  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/booking.html - the booking dialog of the schedule.

  The REAL Bootstrap classes of a modal dialog (.modal, .modal-backdrop...),
  made visible "hard-coded" (show d-block) rather than by the JavaScript of
  Bootstrap. It is the SERVER that decides to display it (&book=... parameter of
  the URL), and closing it amounts to following a link to the same page without this
  parameter.

  The fragment directly reads the variables of the page that includes it
  (booking, doctor_id, day, back_url).

{% load i18n %}
<div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
<div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="booking-title">
  <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
    <form method="post" action="{% url 'schedule_book' %}" class="modal-content">
      <div class="modal-header">
        <h5 class="modal-title" id="booking-title">{% translate "Book this slot" %}</h5>
        <a class="btn-close" href="{{ back_url }}" aria-label="{% translate 'Close' %}"></a>
      </div>

      <div class="modal-body">
        <p>{% blocktranslate with time_range=booking.time_range %}Slot {{ time_range }}{% endblocktranslate %}</p>

        {# what the server must know in addition to the chosen patient #}
        {% csrf_token %}
        <input type="hidden" name="doctorId" value="{{ doctor_id }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="day" value="{{ day }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="slotId" value="{{ booking.slot_id }}">

        {# a patient books for themselves: no list to choose from (and the server ignores any clientId anyway) #}
        {% if booking.patient %}
        <p class="mb-0">
          <span>{% translate "Patient" %}</span>:
          <strong>{{ booking.patient }}</strong>
        </p>
        {% else %}
        <label class="form-label" for="clientId">{% translate "Patient" %}</label>
        <select id="clientId" name="clientId" class="form-select" required autofocus>
          <option value="">{% translate "-- choose a patient --" %}</option>
          {% for client in booking.clients %}
          <option value="{{ client.id }}">{{ client.label }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
        {% endif %}
      </div>

      <div class="modal-footer">
        <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ back_url }}">{% translate "Cancel" %}</a>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Confirm" %}</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>
</div>

    The calendar booking window. It uses the actual classes of a modal window from [Bootstrap] ([modal], [modal-backdrop]...), but made visible "hard-coded" ([show d-block]), rather than via the [JavaScript] from [Bootstrap]: it is the server that decides to display it when URL contains [&book=...]. Closing it (using the X or the Cancel button) is equivalent to following a link to the same page without that parameter ([back_url]).

    • Line 26: [{% blocktranslate with time_range=booking.time_range %}]: a translated text that contains a variable (example 22). In a [blocktranslate], only simple variables are allowed ([{{ time_range }}], not [{{ booking.time_range }}]): the [with] clause creates one;
    • lines 29–32: the anti-CSRF token, and what the server needs to know: the doctor, the day, and the time slot;
    • lines 35–48: a patient makes a reservation for themselves: their name, with no list to choose from (and the server ignores any [clientId] field anyway). The administrator and doctors select the patient from a list; [required] and [autofocus]: the browser requires a selection and places the cursor in the list.

    {% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/captcha.html - the captcha of the authentication page
  (see security/captchas.py). It protects both login and access to the
  account creation (button "Create a patient account"). It reads the variable
  [captcha] of the page.

  captcha.svg|safe: the SVG image is inserted AS IS in the page, without
  escaping. It is safe here because this SVG is made by the server
  itself and contains nothing that comes from the user - one would NEVER do
  that with user input.

  The hidden field captcha_id tells the server WHICH captcha to check; the right
  answer, for its part, is never sent to the browser. "Another image" simply reloads
  the page ({% url 'login' %}: the URL of the page, without its parameters).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="captcha">{% translate "Type the characters shown in the image" %}</label>
  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
    <div class="captcha-image" role="img" aria-label="{% translate 'Anti-robot verification image' %}">{{ captcha.svg|safe }}</div>
    <a class="small" href="{% url 'login' %}">{% translate "Another image" %}</a>
  </div>
  <input type="hidden" name="captcha_id" value="{{ captcha.id }}">
  <input id="captcha" name="captcha" type="text" maxlength="10" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="off"
         spellcheck="false" required class="form-control">
  <div class="form-text">{% translate "Upper or lower case, it does not matter." %}</div>
</div>

    The CAPTCHA (example 27). [captcha.svg|safe] inserts the image SVG as-is, without escaping it: otherwise, the browser would display its code XML. This is safe here because this SVG is generated by the server and contains nothing provided by the user: we would never do this with user input. The hidden field [captcha_id] tells the server which CAPTCHA to verify; the response itself is never sent to the browser. The “Another image” link reloads the login page—and thus the CAPTCHA. The attributes of the input fields ([autocomplete="off"], [autocapitalize="off"], [spellcheck="false"]) prevent the browser from suggesting a previous entry and the phone’s keyboard from capitalizing letters or correcting spelling.

    11.18.2.1. templates/forms/field.html

    {% comment %}
  templates/forms/field.html - a complete field of a form: label,
  input zone, then its error message or its help (see example 18 and the
  FORM_RENDERER setting). The input zone is framed in red (class
  is-invalid) by the flag method of the form (see web/forms.py).
{% endcomment %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="{{ field.id_for_label }}">{{ field.label }}</label>
  {{ field }}
  {% if field.errors %}<div class="invalid-feedback d-block" id="{{ field.auto_id }}_error">{% for error in field.errors %}{{ error }}{% if not forloop.last %}<br>{% endif %}{% endfor %}</div>{% endif %}
  {% if field.help_text and not field.errors %}<div class="form-text" id="{{ field.auto_id }}_helptext">{{ field.help_text }}</div>{% endif %}
</div>

    The template for a complete field—that of the [BootstrapRenderer] rendering engine (web layer, above)—as shown in Example 18: the label, the input field ([{{ field }}], with the classes CSS provided by the form), followed by the error message or, if none, the help text. The classes [invalid-feedback] (the message in red) and [form-text] (the help text in gray) are those of [Bootstrap]; [d-block] displays the message even if the input field is not immediately preceding it. A field may have multiple errors: they are separated by a line break ([forloop.last], example 14).

    The identifiers [..._error] and [..._helptext] are not chosen at random: these are the ones that [Django] refers to in the [aria-describedby] attributes of the input field, with [aria-invalid] for a field with an error. A screen reader thus reads the error message or help text along with the field:

    1
2
3
4
5
    <div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="id_first_name">First name</label>
  <input type="text" name="first_name" maxlength="20" class="form-control is-invalid" required aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="id_first_name_error" id="id_first_name">
  <div class="invalid-feedback d-block" id="id_first_name_error">The first name is required.</div>
</div>

    The red border ([is-invalid]) was added by the form’s [flag] method; [maxlength] and [required] by [Django], based on the field’s options. The [required] attribute does not prevent an empty form from being submitted: the application’s forms carry the [novalidate] attribute (see below); validation is performed by the server.

Each field is rendered by [as_field_group] (Example 18), that is, by the template [field.html]. A page inserts it using [{% include "macros.html#identity" %}]: the fragment reads the variable [form] from the page.

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/login.html - the login form (see web/views/auth.py).
  An ordinary HTML <form>, written by hand: the browser itself sends login,
  password and captcha answer in POST /login, without JavaScript. In case
  of failure, the server sends back THIS page, with the login already entered, a NEW
  captcha and the error, displayed at the bottom of the page by the parent template.
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-sm-8 col-md-6 col-lg-5">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{% translate "Sign in" %}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="{% url 'login' %}">
        {% csrf_token %}
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{% translate "Login" %}</label>
          {# autofocus: a boolean attribute, written if the condition is true. The cursor goes to the first field to fill in #}
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" class="form-control" autocomplete="username"
                 value="{{ login }}" required{% if not login %} autofocus{% endif %}>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">{% translate "Password" %}</label>
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" class="form-control"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required{% if login %} autofocus{% endif %}>
        </div>

        {% include "fragments/captcha.html" %}

        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{% translate "Log in" %}</button>

        {% comment %}
          no account yet: a patient can create one themselves. It is NOT
          a simple link: it is a second submit button of THIS form, which goes
          to another address (formaction). The server checks there the captcha
          above before opening the account creation page (see
          web/views/registration.py). formnovalidate: the browser does not require
          login and password (useless to create an account). Enter in a
          field always triggers the FIRST button of the form, "Log in".
        {% endcomment %}
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-primary w-100 mt-3"
                formaction="{% url 'registration_access' %}" formnovalidate>{% translate "Create a patient account" %}</button>
        <div class="form-text text-center">{% translate "To create an account, first type the characters shown in the image." %}</div>
      </form>

      <div class="text-muted small mt-3">
        <span>{% translate "Demo accounts (password = login):" %}</span>
        <ul class="mb-0 mt-1">
          <li><code>admin</code> - <span>{% translate "ADMIN role: appointments + doctor and patient management" %}</span></li>
          <li><code>pelissier</code>, <code>tatou</code>, <code>dupont</code> - <span>{% translate "DOCTOR role: booking and cancelling appointments" %}</span></li>
          <li><code>martin</code>, <code>durand</code>, <code>bistrou</code>, <code>german</code> - <span>{% translate "USER role (patients): booking for themselves, managing their account" %}</span></li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

    The login form, a hand-coded [<form>], is sent via POST to [/login]. The [{% extends %}] tag is the first in the template (line 1), as required by DTL; the comment follows.

    • Lines 24–30: The entered login is redisplayed after a failed attempt ([login]). The attribute [autofocus] places the cursor in the first field to be filled in: the username if it is empty, the password otherwise (after a failed login attempt or after creating an account). A Boolean attribute is either present or absent: [{% if not login %} autofocus{% endif %}];
    • line 33: the CAPTCHA;
    • lines 46–47: the “Create a patient account” button is not a link; it is a second button that submits the same form to a different address (button attribute [formaction]). The server verifies the CAPTCHA there before opening the account creation page ([registration.access]). [formnovalidate]: The browser does not require a username and password (attributes [required]), as they are not needed to create an account. Pressing the Enter key in a field always triggers the first form submission button: Log in;
    • lines 51–58: demo accounts, for testing.

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/schedule.html - the main page (see web/views/schedule.py).
  Three blocks:
    1. the choice of the doctor and the day;
    2. the schedule;
    3. the booking dialog (booking fragment).
  A possible error (invalid date, unknown doctor) is displayed at the bottom of
  the page by the parent template (error_zone tag).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block content %}
  {# 1. choice of the doctor and the day: a GET form, which simply reloads this page with ?doctorId=...&day=... #}
  <form method="get" action="{% url 'schedule' %}" class="card p-3 mb-3">
    <div class="row g-2 align-items-end">
      <div class="col-sm-5">
        <label class="form-label" for="doctorId">{% translate "Doctor" %}</label>
        <select id="doctorId" name="doctorId" class="form-select" required>
          <option value="">{% translate "-- choose a doctor --" %}</option>
          {% for doctor in doctors %}
          <option value="{{ doctor.id }}"{% if doctor.selected %} selected{% endif %}>{{ doctor.label }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-4">
        <label class="form-label" for="day">{% translate "Day" %}</label>
        <input id="day" name="day" type="date" class="form-control" value="{{ day }}" required>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-3">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{% translate "View schedule" %}</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </form>

  {# patient who already has an upcoming appointment: why there is no "Book" button #}
  {% if info %}
  <div class="alert alert-info">
    <span>{{ info }}</span>
    <a href="{% url 'area' %}" class="alert-link">{% translate "My area" %}</a>
  </div>
  {% endif %}

  {# 2. the schedule #}
  {% if schedule %}
  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{% translate "Schedule for" %} {{ schedule.day }} - {{ schedule.doctor }}</h5>

    {% if schedule.rows %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{% translate "Slot" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "Status" %}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {% for row in schedule.rows %}
        <tr{% if row.bookable %} class="free-slot"{% endif %}>
          <td>{{ row.time_range }}</td>
          <td>
            {% comment %}
              [patient] is only set if the user is allowed to see this
              name (ADMIN, DOCTOR, or the patient for THEIR appointment) - otherwise,
              simply "Booked"
            {% endcomment %}
            {% if row.free %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-success">{% translate "Free" %}</span>
            {% elif row.patient %}
            <span class="badge {% if row.me %}text-bg-primary{% else %}text-bg-secondary{% endif %}">{{ row.patient }}</span>
            {% else %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-secondary">{% translate "Booked" %}</span>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
          <td>
            {% comment %}
              the displayed buttons have been decided by the view (bookable, appointment_id)
              according to the role of the user. "Book" is a simple link: it
              reopens this page with the booking dialog of this slot
            {% endcomment %}
            {% if row.bookable %}
            <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" href="{{ row.book_url }}">{% translate "Book" %}</a>
            {% endif %}
            {# "Cancel" MODIFIES data: it is therefore a POST #}
            {% if row.appointment_id %}
            <form method="post" action="{% url 'schedule_cancel' %}" class="m-0"
                  data-confirmation="{% translate 'Cancel this appointment?' %}">
              {% csrf_token %}
              <input type="hidden" name="appointmentId" value="{{ row.appointment_id }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="doctorId" value="{{ doctor_id }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="day" value="{{ day }}">
              <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{% translate "Cancel" %}</button>
            </form>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{% translate "This doctor has no time slots." %}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
  {% else %}
  <p class="text-muted">{% translate 'Choose a doctor and a day, then click "View schedule".' %}</p>
  {% endif %}

  {# 3. the booking dialog, only if the URL contains &book=... #}
  {% if booking %}
  {% include "fragments/booking.html" %}
  {% endif %}
{% endblock %}

    The main page. Three sections: selecting a doctor and a day, the calendar, and the booking window.

    • Lines 17–36: Selecting a doctor and a day: a GET form (example 17), which reloads the page with [?doctorId=...&day=...] in the URL. The day is a [type="date"] field: the browser displays a calendar and sends the date in [yyyy-mm-dd] format, regardless of how it displays it ([30/09/2026] in French); the initial value ([value]) is written in this same format;
    • lines 39–44: for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment, why there is no “Book” button, with a link to “My area”;
    • Lines 70–76: The slot status: Free (in green), the patient’s name (in blue for an appointment booked by the logged-in patient, in gray otherwise), or “Booked.” The template does not determine anything: [row.patient] is only displayed if the user has permission to view that name;
    • lines 84–86: “Book” is a simple link: it reopens the page with the reservation window for that time slot ([row.book_url]). It does not modify anything: a GET is sufficient;
    • lines 88–97: “Cancel” modifies data: it is a POST form (example 21), with its anti-CSRF token, the appointment to be canceled, and information to return to the same page (the doctor, the day). The [data-confirmation] attribute causes the page’s script to request confirmation; its text is represented by [{% translate %}], enclosed in single quotes within the attribute, which is itself enclosed in double quotes;
    • lines 112–114: the booking window, if URL requests it (and if the time slot is bookable).

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/persons/list.html - the list of the doctors OR of the clients (ADMIN).
  A single template for both: the texts specific to each one arrive in
  [texts], and [section] ("doctors" or "clients") gives the start of the names of the
  routes (see web/views/persons.py).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block content %}
  <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
    <h4 class="mb-0">{{ texts.title }}</h4>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="{{ add_url }}">{{ texts.add }}</a>
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3">
    {% if persons %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle mb-0">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{% translate "Title" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "First name" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "Last name" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "Login" %}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {# person.account.login: the account, loaded by the same query (select_related) #}
        {% for person in persons %}
        <tr>
          <td>{{ person.title }}</td>
          <td>{{ person.first_name }}</td>
          <td>{{ person.last_name }}</td>
          <td><code>{{ person.account.login }}</code></td>
          <td class="text-end">
            <div class="d-inline-flex gap-2">
              {# section|add:"_edit": "doctors_edit", the name of the route #}
              <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary"
                 href="{% url section|add:'_edit' person.id %}">{% translate "Edit" %}</a>
              {# data-confirmation: a confirmation dialog will open before the form is sent (see static/js/app.js) #}
              <form method="post" action="{% url section|add:'_delete' person.id %}" class="m-0"
                    data-confirmation="{{ texts.confirm_delete }}">
                {% csrf_token %}
                <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{% translate "Delete" %}</button>
              </form>
            </div>
          </td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ texts.empty }}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}

    The list of doctors or clients: the text specific to each one is stored in the variable [texts], and the route names are generated from the section name: [section|add:'_edit'] yields [doctors_edit] or [clients_edit] (the filter [add] adds two numbers or, as in this case, concatenates two strings). [{% url %}] thus accepts, as a route name, a calculated expression followed by the route parameters ([person.id]). [person.account.login]: the account login, loaded along with the list (layer DAO), and stored with it in the cache. The Delete button is a POST form, with confirmation.

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/persons/form.html - creation OR update of a doctor or
  a client (ADMIN), with the PersonForm form.

  When the input is refused (empty field, login already taken...), the view displays
  THIS page again, and the template shows:
    - the values already entered (except the password);
    - the faulty fields framed in red (Bootstrap class "is-invalid");
    - under a field refused by the validation, its message;
    - the error message of the page, AT THE BOTTOM of the page (error_zone tag).
  The form is sent to the URL of the page itself (no action attribute).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ page_title }}</h5>

      <form method="post" novalidate>
        {% csrf_token %}
        {# title, first name, last name: a fragment common to three forms #}
        {% include "macros.html#identity" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{% translate "User account" %}</h6>
        {{ form.login.as_field_group }}
        {# never pre-filled: the password never goes back to the browser #}
        {{ form.password.as_field_group }}
        {# in update mode only: the version of the record, in a hidden field (the optimistic lock) #}
        {% if form.version %}{{ form.version }}{% endif %}

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-4">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Save" %}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ list_url }}">{% translate "Back to the list" %}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

    Creating or modifying a doctor or a client using the [PersonForm] form.

    • Line 24: a POST form without the [action] attribute: it is sent to the URL of the page itself ([/doctors/add] or [/doctors/3/edit]). [novalidate] disables browser validation ([required], [maxlength]...) when the form is submitted: the server performs the validation, and its result is authoritative (example 19);
    • line 27: title, first name, and last name, via the fragment [identity];
    • lines 30–32: the username and password, which are never pre-filled. Their tooltips differ between creation and modification (depending on the form builder);
    • line 34: for editing only, the hidden version field (the optimistic lock). [{{ form.version }}] populates the input field alone, without a label: [<input type="hidden" name="version" value="1" id="id_version">]. When creating a record, the form does not have a [version] field: the variable is empty, and the test evaluates to false.

    Errors in the form itself that do not involve any fields ([non_field_errors], example 19) do not need to be displayed: the form does not generate any, and an invalid anti-CSRF token is rejected before the view (the 419 page).

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/registration.html - "Create a patient account" (public page, see
  web/views/registration.py), with the RegistrationForm form. Same identity
  fields as the ADMIN form (identity fragment), but the login and the
  password are required, with confirmation. No captcha HERE: this page
  is only reached after typing the one of the
  authentication page ("Create a patient account" button).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-1">{% translate "Create a patient account" %}</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small mb-3">{% translate "With this account you can book your own appointments." %}</p>

      <form method="post" action="{% url 'registration' %}" novalidate>
        {% csrf_token %}
        {% include "macros.html#identity" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{% translate "User account" %}</h6>
        {{ form.login.as_field_group }}
        {# the password and its confirmation, side by side #}
        <div class="row g-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ form.password.as_field_group }}</div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ form.confirmation.as_field_group }}</div>
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-3">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Create my account" %}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{% url 'login' %}">{% translate "Back to login" %}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

    Creating a patient account: the identity fields, followed by the username, password, and password confirmation—all required fields—side by side (lines 28–31). The password help text specifies the minimum length: “At least 6 characters.” There is no CAPTCHA here: you can only reach this page after entering the CAPTCHA from the login page.

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/area.html - "My area": the home page of the patient (USER role),
  displayed just after they log in.
    - two options: [Manage my account] and [View a schedule];
    - their upcoming appointment, if they have one, with the means to cancel it.
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block content %}
  <h4 class="mb-3">{% blocktranslate %}Hello {{ patient }}{% endblocktranslate %}</h4>

  <div class="row g-3 mb-4">
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <a class="card p-4 h-100 text-decoration-none option-card" href="{% url 'account' %}">
        <h5 class="mb-1">{% translate "Manage my account" %}</h5>
        <span class="text-muted">{% translate "Change my details or password, or delete my account." %}</span>
      </a>
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <a class="card p-4 h-100 text-decoration-none option-card" href="{% url 'schedule' %}">
        <h5 class="mb-1">{% translate "View a schedule" %}</h5>
        <span class="text-muted">{% translate "See a doctor's schedule and book a slot." %}</span>
      </a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{% translate "My appointment" %}</h5>
    {% comment %}
      normally only one (rule "one upcoming appointment at a time"), but the page
      can display several. {% for %} ... {% empty %}: a loop, and what
      is displayed if the list is empty; forloop.last: last element?
    {% endcomment %}
    {% for appointment in appointments %}
    <div class="d-flex flex-wrap justify-content-between align-items-center gap-2 py-2{% if not forloop.last %} border-bottom{% endif %}">
      <div>
        <div class="fw-semibold">{{ appointment.day }}, {{ appointment.time_range }}</div>
        <div class="text-muted">
          <span>{{ appointment.doctor }}</span> -
          <a href="{{ appointment.schedule_url }}">{% translate "see in the schedule" %}</a>
        </div>
      </div>
      <form method="post" action="{% url 'area_cancel' %}" class="m-0"
            data-confirmation="{% translate 'Cancel this appointment?' %}">
        {% csrf_token %}
        <input type="hidden" name="appointmentId" value="{{ appointment.id }}">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-danger">{% translate "Cancel this appointment" %}</button>
      </form>
    </div>
    {% empty %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{% translate "You have no upcoming appointment." %}</p>
    {% endfor %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}

    “My area,” the patient’s home page: two large cards (“Manage my account,” “View a schedule”), and their upcoming appointment.

    • line 13: [{% blocktranslate %}Hello {{ patient }}{% endblocktranslate %}]: a translated text containing a variable ([Bonjour %(patient)s] in the French dictionary);
    • lines 37–55: [{% for %}] ... [{% empty %}] (Example 14) is a loop, followed by what to display if the list is empty. Normally, a patient has at most one upcoming appointment; however, the page is capable of displaying multiple appointments. [forloop.last] (Example 14): the last item has no separator;
    • lines 46–51: each appointment has a cancellation form (POST, with confirmation), which sends only its ID: the server will verify that it belongs to the logged-in patient.

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/account.html - "Manage my account" (USER role). Two independent
  forms on the same page:
    1. the update (identity, login, optional new password), with
       the MyAccountForm form;
    2. the deletion of the account - which also cancels its appointments: a
       form written by hand.
  Both require the CURRENT password (current_password field).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">

    {# 1. update; novalidate: it is the SERVER that validates (see example 19) #}
    <div class="card p-4 mb-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{% translate "Manage my account" %}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="{% url 'account' %}" novalidate>
        {% csrf_token %}
        {% include "macros.html#identity" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{% translate "User account" %}</h6>
        {{ form.login.as_field_group }}
        <div class="row g-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ form.password.as_field_group }}</div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ form.confirmation.as_field_group }}</div>
        </div>
        {{ form.current_password.as_field_group }}
        {# the version of the record: a hidden field (the optimistic lock) #}
        {{ form.version }}

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-4">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Save" %}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{% url 'area' %}">{% translate "Back to my area" %}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>

    {% comment %}
      2. deletion. The password field has the same NAME as that of the first
      form (current_password), but another id: two elements of the same
      page cannot have the same id
    {% endcomment %}
    <div class="card p-4 border-danger">
      <h5 class="card-title text-danger mb-1">{% translate "Delete my account" %}</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small">{% translate "Your account will be permanently deleted, together with all your appointments." %}</p>
      <form method="post" action="{% url 'account_delete' %}" class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-2 align-items-end"
            data-confirmation="{% translate 'Permanently delete your account? Any appointment you have will be cancelled.' %}">
        {% csrf_token %}
        <div class="flex-grow-1">
          <label class="form-label" for="delete_password">{% translate "Current password" %}</label>
          <input id="delete_password" name="current_password" type="password" maxlength="72"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required class="form-control">
        </div>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-danger">{% translate "Delete my account" %}</button>
      </form>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

    “Manage my account”: two independent forms on the same page.

    • Lines 20–42: the update, using the [MyAccountForm] form: the identity fields, the login, the new password and its confirmation (optional), the current password (required), and the hidden version field;
    • Lines 49–62: Account deletion, a handwritten form with its own field for the current password and a confirmation field. The field has the same name as the one on the first form ([current_password]), but a different ID: two elements on a page cannot have the same ID, as indicated by the attribute [for] for a label. The two forms are independent: the browser sends only the fields from the form whose button was clicked.

    11.19. Static files

    The [static] folder contains the files that the server sends as-is (example 15): [Bootstrap] ([lib/bootstrap], the stylesheet alone, and its license), a stylesheet, and a script. During development, the [Django] server serves them itself ([django.contrib.staticfiles] application); in production, they are copied to [var/static] by the command [collectstatic], and served by the web server (“A production server”).

    /* =========================================================================
   static/css/styles.css - a few settings on top of Bootstrap
   (the same as in the other versions of this application).
   ========================================================================= */

body {
  background-color: #f5f7fa;
}

.free-slot:hover {
  background-color: #e9f7ef;
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   .error-zone: the error messages, at the bottom of the page, on a light pink background
   (see templates/fragments/errors.html).
   position: sticky + bottom: if the page is taller than the window (a
   schedule of 12 slots, for example), the zone stays stuck to the bottom of the
   window instead of disappearing below the fold - without ever
   covering the content when the page is short.
   z-index: above the grey background of the booking dialog (.modal-backdrop).
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
.error-zone {
  position: sticky;
  bottom: 1rem;
  z-index: 1060;
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  padding: 0.75rem 1rem;
  background-color: #fdecef; /* light pink */
  border: 1px solid #f5c2c7;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
  color: #842029;
}

/* the two big options of the patient's "My area" page */
.option-card {
  transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s;
}

.option-card:hover {
  border-color: #0d6efd;
  box-shadow: 0 0.25rem 0.75rem rgba(13, 110, 253, 0.15);
}

/* the captcha image (SVG of 150 x 50 pixels) */
.captcha-image svg {
  display: block;
  border: 1px solid #dee2e6;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
}

    A few additional settings for [Bootstrap], the same as in the other versions of the application.

    • lines 10–12: a bookable slot in the calendar turns green on mouseover;
    • lines 23–33: the error area at the bottom of the page has a light pink background. [position: sticky] with [bottom: 1rem]: if the page is taller than the window (a calendar with 12 time slots), the area remains anchored to the bottom of the window instead of disappearing below the scroll bar; if the page is short, it stays in place without covering anything. [z-index]: It appears over the gray background of the booking window;
    • lines 36–43: the two large “My area” cards, which light up when the mouse hovers over them;
    • lines 46–50: the CAPTCHA image, with a border.

    // =========================================================================
// static/js/app.js - the ONLY JavaScript of the application.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The whole application works without JavaScript. This script adds a
// convenience: before sending a form that carries the attribute
// data-confirmation="...", a modal dialog asks "Are you sure?"
// (the dialog itself is in the page: templates/fragments/confirmation.html).
// If JavaScript is disabled, the form is simply sent without
// confirmation - nothing breaks ("progressive enhancement" principle).
//
// Why not window.confirm()? Its box cannot be styled, and its
// buttons stay in the language of the browser, not in that of the page.
// =========================================================================

(() => {
  const modal = document.getElementById('confirmation-modal');
  if (!modal) {
    return;
  }
  const message = document.getElementById('confirmation-modal-message');
  const noButton = modal.querySelector('.modal-footer [data-action="no"]');

  let pendingForm = null; // the form to send if the user confirms
  let previousFocus = null; // the element to give the focus back to on closing

  function open(form) {
    pendingForm = form;
    previousFocus = document.activeElement;
    // textContent (and not innerHTML): the message is displayed as TEXT,
    // never interpreted as HTML
    message.textContent = form.dataset.confirmation;
    modal.classList.remove('d-none');
    // the focus goes on "No": an absent-minded press on Enter deletes nothing
    noButton.focus();
  }

  function close() {
    modal.classList.add('d-none');
    pendingForm = null;
    if (previousFocus) {
      previousFocus.focus();
    }
  }

  // 1. we intercept the sending of the forms to confirm
  document.querySelectorAll('form[data-confirmation]').forEach((form) => {
    form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
      event.preventDefault();
      open(form);
    });
  });

  // 2. the buttons of the dialog (Yes / No / close cross)
  modal.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
    const action = event.target.closest('[data-action]')?.dataset.action;
    if (action === 'yes') {
      const form = pendingForm;
      close();
      // form.submit() sends the form WITHOUT triggering the
      // 'submit' event again: no new confirmation request
      form.submit();
    } else if (action === 'no') {
      close();
    } else if (event.target.classList.contains('modal')) {
      close(); // click on the grey background, outside the dialog
    }
  });

  // 3. keyboard: Escape closes the dialog; Tab stays INSIDE the dialog
  //    (otherwise the focus would go to the greyed-out page, behind)
  modal.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
    if (event.key === 'Escape') {
      close();
    } else if (event.key === 'Tab') {
      const buttons = [...modal.querySelectorAll('button')];
      const first = buttons[0];
      const last = buttons[buttons.length - 1];
      if (event.shiftKey && document.activeElement === first) {
        event.preventDefault();
        last.focus();
      } else if (!event.shiftKey && document.activeElement === last) {
        event.preventDefault();
        first.focus();
      }
    }
  });
})();

    The only [JavaScript] in the application—the one from Example 21—with a few additions. The entire application works without [JavaScript]: this script adds convenience by providing a confirmation before submitting a form that carries the [data-confirmation] attribute. If [JavaScript] is disabled, the form submits without confirmation: nothing breaks (principle of progressive enhancement).

    • Lines 15–19: The script is a function called as soon as it is defined ([(() => { ... })()]); its variables are not visible to the rest of the page. Without a confirmation window on the page, it does nothing;
    • Lines 26–35: Opening the window: the form to be submitted if the user confirms is stored, and the form’s message is displayed in the window. [textContent], not [innerHTML]: the message is displayed as text and is never interpreted as HTML. Focus moves to the “No” button: accidentally pressing Enter does not delete anything;
    • lines 37–43: closing the window; focus returns to the element that had it previously;
    • lines 46–51: the submission of each form to be confirmed is intercepted ([preventDefault] prevents it), and the window opens. The [submit] event occurs only after the browser’s validations: the current password, which is required ([required]) in the account deletion form, is required before the prompt;
    • lines 54–67: the buttons in the window. A single handler for the entire window: [closest('[data-action]')] finds the clicked button or the element containing it; [?.] ensures [undefined] returns no error if none match. “Yes” submits the form via [form.submit()], which does not trigger the [submit] event: no new confirmation prompt appears. Clicking on the grayed-out background outside the window closes it;
    • lines 71–86: the keyboard. Esc closes the window; the Tab key moves the focus from one button to another without leaving the window (otherwise, it would move to the grayed-out page behind it): this is what users who navigate with the keyboard and screen readers expect.
